 Dutch petrol prices fall to lowest level since March, diesel cheapest since July 
 Wednesday, 11 November 2026 - 19:30
 Fuel prices in the Netherlands have dropped to their lowest point since March, driven largely by falling oil prices. Investors have grown more optimistic about the possibility of a diplomatic resolution to the conflict in the Middle East.
 UnitedConsumers, a Dutch consumer savings platform, reported that the recommended petrol price dropped by more than 2 cents per liter on Wednesday, reaching 2.420 euros. It is the lowest level since March, when the start of the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz triggered a sharp increase in fuel prices.
 Diesel prices fell even further, dropping by more than 4 cents per liter on Wednesday to 2.525 euros, their lowest point since July. These recommended prices are typically charged at more expensive petrol stations, particularly those along highways, while other stations can offer fuel for several dozen cents less.
 Oil prices fell below 90 dollars per barrel this week after U.S. President Donald Trump said there was no need for further attacks on Iran. The decline came despite continued unrest in the Middle East. The Democrats' victory in last week's midterm elections has also helped change investor sentiment.
 Oil prices rose slightly again on Wednesday, as there were still no clear indications that a peace deal was close. An analyst at Raymond James & Associates warned that even if the two sides reach a lasting agreement, it is likely to be a messy compromise that leaves many issues unresolved.
 Reporting by ANP
